newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels threaten to hang looters in Bukavu.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels threaten to hang looters in Bukavu.

text.p: Rebels holding the east Zaire city of Bukavu, scene of fierce fighting earlier this week, on Saturday sought to impose their authority posting guards outside shops and warning that looters would be hanged.
Tutsi rebels captured Bukavu, capital of South Kivu province, after battles with the Zairean army on Tuesday and Wednesday.

Corpses still litter the streets. Body counts by priests and journalists suggest that at least 83 people died in the fighting and probably many more. Among the dead was Roman Catholic Archbishop Christophe Munzihirwa.
Bukavu has no electricity and little food or water but Zaireans are gradually trickling back to the city, where a rebel spokesman addressed about 2,000 people on Saturday.

The spokesman, who gave his name only as Masusu, said: "Don't be afraid of our army. We are not the same as the army we have driven out. We are not going to steal and loot from you as they did. We are ordering that the looting stop."
Masusu told the audience, which included Pakistani, Indian and Lebanese businessmen, that looters would be hanged.
There has been comparatively little looting in Bukavu since ill-disciplined Zairean troops fled.
Three days after the final battle for Bukavu priests were still burying the dead. An Italian priest said that in the city's Nwera district alone 40 people had been buried.
Twelve people were buried in a communal grave in a northern part of the city called La Botte and in a primary school lay the bodies of seven Zairean soldiers who had been shot dead.
On Saturday a convoy of 11 vehicles carrying 74 people, including priests and businessmen, pulled out of Bukavu heading for the Rwandan capital of Kigali.
The convoy, organised by the honorary Belgian consul Michel van Kerckhove, took out 10 Belgians, eight Italians, six Spaniards and other foreigners and Zaireans.
But a number of Lebanese and Indian businessmen stayed. The rebels have posted armed guards in front of their shops.
On Saturday the distant sound of explosions could be heard to the north of the city, but there were no signs of Zairean troops close to Bukavu.
